name: NA62
summary: NA62 is based in the CERN SPS North Area, Prévessin. The rare-kaon experiment also conducts actual dark-sector beam-mode runs; its full normal kaon-decay exposure is not dark-matter exposure.
detection_principle: Alongside rare charged-kaon decays, a proton-beam-dump mode produces weakly coupled particles sought as displaced electron- or muon-pair decay vertices behind shielding; invisible-dark-photon searches in π⁰ decays are also conducted.

results.summary: Dilepton-decay searches found no signal; combined electron and muon channels constrain dark photons. Mass/mixing coverage must be read within the paper's models and lifetime intervals.

science_scope: Tests dark-sector models by producing candidate particles or portal mediators at accelerators. Invisible accelerator final states or mediator particles alone do not establish cosmic-dark-matter identity; lifetimes, abundance and other experiments must also be considered.
